thread:
mira: Quick follow-up from today's infra all-hands. Putting questions about GPU inventory, regional prioritization, and autoscaler behavior into one thread so we can action them. I'll track owners and post links.

jordan: Appreciate it. Which APAC zones are we targeting exactly? Any estimate for first A100 arrivals and how they'll be staged (small batch vs full rack)?

mira: APAC target prologue: SIN (Singapore) and NRT (Tokyo) first, then SYD. Initial arrivals will be small racks (2-4 nodes) for verification, then full racks if procurement windows hold. Current supplier ETA: small waves mid-June, bulk late July. Still some uncertainty on freight windows.

dom: For Dedicated: if a customer's reserved pool is full and we need to serve emergency traffic, are we allowed to overflow into on-demand with a different model variant, or do we guarantee strict isolation? Concerned about latency cliffs for sync endpoints.

mira: Reserved pools are hard-isolated for committed customers. Overflow into on-demand only happens for soft-reservation tiers (reserved+burst). In that case we route to a compatible quantized variant (q8/q4) with clear SLO deltas. We will not fallback to CPU for low-latency sync routes; CPU fallback remains for async jobs only.

sam: Who's owning the observability knobs for the canary? Need trace sampling, token-latency histograms, and a per-variant error budget display in console.

leila: Runtime + Ops (me + Pat) will own the rollout. Platform will add console widgets. Pat, can you confirm the canary cadence and monitoring thresholds?

pat: Canary plan: 4-step ramp per region (0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 100%). Hold time: 20m between steps for quick checks, longer soak on the 10% step (2h). Alerts: error rate > 0.5% absolute or 3x baseline, p95 token latency regress > 40ms relative. Rolling back if thresholds trip. I'll post the runbook and the k6 scenarios here.

kyle: We've seen autoscaler thrash when a zone returns capacity quickly. Any change to cooldown/scale delta?

mira: Yes, we adjusted scale-down cooldown to +90s and added a 2-minute stabilization window after significant upticks. Also introduced dynamic hysteresis based on request QPS variance. Change is in canary in staging.

ina: billing question: how will burst usage surface on invoices for Dedicated customers who pay monthly commits?

ina: sorry, meant ina (typo)

ina: ^^ still me

mira: By default bursts are billed as on-demand. For enterprise deals we can put burst buffers into the contract (pre-bought buffer or capped billing). Finance will prepare example scenarios for common commit sizes.

ops-bot: deploy started: canary/variant-routing -> SIN at 1946012346 by pat

jordan: Could we get a sample routing policy? a simple YAML would help teams define fallbacks and understand expected latencies.

dom: +1 for a clear SLO table per variant (primary, q8, q4, q2).

pat: Sample policy (YAML) below, drop-in for platform rules:
---
route: model-fallback
primary: biggen-v2
fallbacks:
  - biggen-v2-q8
  - biggen-v2-q4
latency_ms:
  primary: "<70"
  q8: "<110"
  q4: "<180"
max_fallback_pct: "20%"
soak_policy: "progressive"
---
Use this to simulate in the staging router.

mira: Action items from thread: 1) Pat & Leila: publish canary runbook + k6 scripts (ETA: EOD tomorrow). 2) Platform: add sample routing YAML + SLO table to docs site (ETA: 3 business days). 3) Finance: publish burst-pricing examples for Dedicated customers (ETA: next week). 4) Capacity team: update capacity dashboard with APAC micro-waves timeline (ETA: update by Friday). I'll collate and attach links when ready.

jordan: My team can run a controlled cross-region soak on Friday night to exercise the autoscaler. We'll coordinate windows so it's non-disruptive.

pat: Thanks — please DM the test plan. We'll schedule a quiet window and thread the incidents channel if needed.

mira: Great. I'll follow up with a compiled FAQ and owners. Ping me or @leila for anything urgent. :thumbsup:
